clues: This is a warm isle in Brazil, just off the shore in Pernambuco state. A salt sea channel splits it from the mainland, and a long bridge joins them back.
It stays warm all year, with temps in a tight range day after day. Then hard rains come in the wet months from May through July each year.
For most of its past, this place did not hold full city rank at all. It gained that rank at last on New Year's Day in 1959.
Two thirds of this place is wild rain forest that the law keeps safe. Most homes crowd on a thin strip of land by the white sand shore.
A reef rings the sea side here and keeps the shore water shallow, safe, and warm. White sand beaches stretch a long way down its east coast.
